The dataset seems generally clean with no empty value and has a total of 216946 entries

Features such as 'lease_commence_date' and 'remaining_lease' do not seems to carry much value to the data set. Furthermore, 'remaining_lease' will differ based on the year it is updated so it may be outdated.

Added new feature 'remaining_lease_years' to identify the remaining lease year of the flat

Given the nature of the dataset with different 'flat_model' and 'flat_type', 'resale_price' and 'floor_area_sqm' would be better represented 'price_per_sqm' to understand the cost of each square metre for each flat to provide better comparison.

Hence, dropped 'resale_price' and 'floor_area_sqm', and added new feature 'price_per_sqm'

Part 2: EDA¶

Plot 1: Number of Transaction per Town (%)¶

Based on the bar graph, Sengkang has the most number of sales from year 2017 to 2025. This could be due to the effect of houses being TOP and younger folks upgrading their flat.

Plot 2: Number of Transaction per Flat Model (%)¶

Based on the bar graph, Model A,HDB flats that have two separate levels, has the most number of transactions. Possibly due to older folks wanting a smaller area and younger folks wanting a larger space

Plot 3: Number of Transaction per Storey Range (%)¶

Based on the bar graph, storey range of 4-9 has the most number of transactions

Plot 4: Distribution of Remaining Years¶

Based on the distribution table, most of the transaction are houses with remaining year of 55-65 and 85-90 years.

For flats with 85-90 remaining years, transaction could be due house being TOP and people upgrading their flat to private houses

Plot 5: Number of Transaction per Year (%)¶

Based on the bar graph, year 2021 and 2024 have the highest number of transactions.

2021 surge could be due to COVID 19 where new flat BTO was delayed causing families to buy resale instead.

2024 surge could be due to the rising interest rate where people rush to buy HDB flat as interest rate to fund private houses are more expensive

Plot 6: Distribution of Resale Prices by Storey Range¶

Based on the voilin plot, it is seem that the resale price per sqm increases with the storey range. Meaning that houses at higher floor fetch higher resale price per sqm

Categorical feature encoding

  1. one-hot encode for 'town', 'flat_type', 'flat_model' as it is a nominal categorical data.

  2. ordinal encode for 'storey_range' as it has a ordinal relationship.

Plot 7: Correlation Matrix¶

Assuming all relationship between features are linear, correlatiom matrix is plotted to identify if 2 features are positive, negative or not correlated.

  • if box color is towards red, it means features are positive correlated, when 1 increase, another will also increase.
  • if box color is towards blue, it means features are negative correlated, when 1 increase,, another will decerease. vice versa.
  • if box color is neutral, it means that features are not correlated. Both features move at either same or different direction.

Based on the plot above, focusing on the price per sqm:

  • Positive correlated with price per sqm

    • storey range (support evidence in plot 6 that price increase when storey increase)
    • remaining lease** year (this is generally so as people who buy the flat can stay there longer so more expensive)

  • Negative correlation with price per sqm

    • new generation flat type (new generation flat decrease with price per sqm as it has lesser demand as lesser people are eligible for such flat)
    • woodlands and chua chu kang (house in these area have a low price per sqm)

  • No correlation with price per sqm

    • houses in bukit merah town (houses sold here has no correlation with the price per sqm. This means that resale prices are not affected irregardless of sqm)
